subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Floating Point: Decimals in Binary
description: One-minute skill: Floating Point: Decimals in Binary.

hook.text: Integers are easy in binary. But how do computers handle 3.14 or 0.001?

buildup.text: Floating point splits a number into sign, exponent, and mantissa — like scientific notation.

discovery.text: IEEE 754 defines 32-bit and 64-bit formats. Every computer follows the same standard.

twist.text: 0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3 in floating point — tiny rounding errors are inevitable.

climax.text: Graphics, physics simulations, and AI training all depend on fast floating-point hardware.

punchline.text: Computers approximate decimals — close for rockets, tricky for banks.

quiz.question: Why does 0.1 + 0.2 not equal exactly 0.3 in floating point?
options: Computers can't add numbers smaller than 1
Some decimal fractions can't be represented exactly in binary, causing tiny rounding errors
The IEEE 754 standard intentionally rounds all results down
